intent: Let clients optionally set an expiry in days when creating a short link, so that the redirect for an expired link returns 410 Gone instead of redirecting, while links created without an expiry never expire.

functional_needs.statement: POST /api/links accepts an optional expiry value, expressed in days, alongside the URL when a short link is created.
functional_needs.source_quote: when creating a short link the client may give an expiry in days

functional_needs.statement: Once a link's expiry time has passed, GET /{code} for that link returns 410 Gone instead of a 302 redirect. The response uses the existing application/problem+json error format.
functional_needs.source_quote: After it expires, the redirect returns 410 Gone instead of redirecting

functional_needs.statement: Before its expiry time, a link with an expiry keeps redirecting as it does today: 302, Location set to the long URL, and Cache-Control: no-store.
functional_needs.source_quote: After it expires, the redirect returns 410 Gone

functional_needs.statement: Links created without an expiry never expire. A create request that omits the expiry field still returns 201 with the same Location header and body fields as today, and the link keeps redirecting indefinitely.
functional_needs.source_quote: Links without an expiry never expire

functional_needs.statement: Links that existed before this change have no expiry. They keep working for redirect, details and analytics on upgraded deployments without errors.
functional_needs.source_quote: Links without an expiry never expire

functional_needs.statement: GET /{code} for an unknown code still returns 404, not 410. Only known links whose expiry has passed return 410.
functional_needs.source_quote: the redirect returns 410 Gone instead of redirecting

ambiguities.question: Which expiry values are valid, and what happens with invalid ones (zero, negative, fractional, numeric strings like "7", or very large numbers)?
ambiguities.why_it_matters: This determines which create requests return 201 and which return 400. Very large values could otherwise cause 500 errors or corrupt the stored expiry. A rejected request must not persist a link.
ambiguities.recommended_default: Accept only whole-number JSON integers from 1 to 3650 inclusive. Reject zero, negative, fractional, string and out-of-range values with 400 application/problem+json whose detail describes the expiry problem. Persist nothing on rejection.
options: Whole-number integers 1–3650; everything else returns 400 and nothing is persisted
Any positive integer up to a larger maximum (e.g. 36500); everything else returns 400
Lenient: accept numeric strings and truncate fractions, rejecting only zero, negative and out-of-range values

ambiguities.question: Should a GET /{code} that returns 410 for an expired link increase the click count or update the last-click time?
ambiguities.why_it_matters: This changes the clickCount and lastClickedAt values that the analytics endpoint returns for expired links.
ambiguities.recommended_default: No. Only successful 302 redirects are counted. A 410 response leaves clickCount and lastClickedAt unchanged.
options: Not counted: 410 responses leave the analytics unchanged
Counted: every access attempt to a known link increments clickCount

ambiguities.question: What should GET /api/links/{code} and GET /api/links/{code}/analytics return for an expired link?
ambiguities.why_it_matters: Returning 410 there would change the existing contracts of those endpoints. Returning 200 keeps details and analytics viewable after expiry.
ambiguities.recommended_default: Keep returning 200 with the current fields. Only the redirect endpoint returns 410.
options: 200 with current fields (only the redirect returns 410)
410 Gone on details and analytics as well

ambiguities.question: Should the create and details responses expose the computed expiry time?
ambiguities.why_it_matters: Clients cannot see when a link expires unless the response includes it. Adding the field is additive, but a null value for non-expiring links is visible to strict clients.
ambiguities.recommended_default: Add an expiresAt field (UTC timestamp) to the create and details responses. It is null for links without an expiry, and this is documented.
options: Add expiresAt, null when the link never expires
Add expiresAt, omitted when the link never expires
Do not expose the expiry in responses

ambiguities.question: How is 'days' measured, and is a link expired exactly at its expiry instant?
ambiguities.why_it_matters: This defines precisely when the redirect switches from 302 to 410.
ambiguities.recommended_default: expiresAt = createdAt + N × 24 hours (UTC). The link is expired when the current time is at or after expiresAt.
options: N × 24h from createdAt; expired when now >= expiresAt
N × 24h from createdAt; expired when now > expiresAt
Expire at the end of the Nth calendar day (UTC)

ambiguities.question: What should the request field for the expiry be named, and does an explicit null count as no expiry?
ambiguities.why_it_matters: The field name is part of the public API contract that clients must use.
ambiguities.recommended_default: Name it expiresInDays. Treat an absent field and an explicit null the same way: the link never expires. Continue to ignore unknown JSON properties.
options: expiresInDays; null is treated as absent
expiryDays; null is treated as absent

out_of_scope: Changing or removing a link's expiry after creation
Deleting or purging expired links from storage
Specifying expiry as an absolute timestamp or in units other than days
Making expiry mandatory or applying a default expiry to links
Custom aliases, authentication, or any other change to existing endpoints beyond the expiry behaviour
